title: etl4/vault/compact.py: compact_small_hub -- replaces inline _compact_small_hub stub for the 3 non-partitioned hubs
objective: New module etl4/vault/compact.py honouring the pinned 10-item contract from the T-11 vault review section E. compact_small_hub(name, new_frames, out_dir) -> int reads new-month hub frames, unions with the existing monolith, dedups on the business key with existing-first precedence, and writes back atomically. Replaces the inline _compact_small_hub stub in raw_vault.py (now a one-line wrapper).

files_changed.note: Public API compact_small_hub + DEDUP_KEYS. Duplicates _dedup_safely with pyarrow 2 GiB detour (object round-trip). Handles four empty/non-empty branches explicitly: existing+empty is a byte-identical no-op, no monolith+empty writes an empty monolith, non-empty paths union existing-first + dedup + atomic write.

Surgical: ONLY the body of _compact_small_hub and its stale 4-line T-09 marker comment (which became false). The function is now a one-line wrapper `from etl4.vault.compact import compact_small_hub; return compact_small_hub(...)`. Import kept inside the function body to leave top-level imports untouched. _atomic_write_monolith + the module-level _dedup_safely are now unused dead code (see RISKS -- intentionally left in place to keep this edit surgical).

10 case functions exercising every contract item + a case 10 that replays the T-08 head(5000) two-month fixture through compact.py alone and asserts the baseline row counts (hub_aircraft=8355, hub_airport=1124, sat_aircraft_identity=8355). No DB; tempdir fixtures only. ASCII only in every print.

contract_deviations: Orchestrator brief's skeleton showed `_DEDUP_KEYS['sat_aircraft_identity'] = ['hk_aircraft_identity']`. That column does not exist on the production frame (`build_sat_aircraft_identity` emits hk_aircraft, load_dt, rec_src, registration, typecode). Using it would raise KeyError in _dedup_safely. Implementation uses `['hk_aircraft']` which matches raw_vault._FINAL_DEDUP['sat_aircraft_identity'] and T-11 section E item 6 ('do NOT redefine'). Smoke case 1 asserts DEDUP_KEYS == _FINAL_DEDUP slice for all three tables so a future drift would fail loudly.

Orchestrator brief item 4 says `new_frames=[]` returns the existing hub unchanged. Implementation treats this literally: when the monolith already exists and no non-empty frame is present, compact_small_hub returns the parquet footer row count WITHOUT rewriting the file. mtime + SHA preserved. This strengthens the T-08 inline stub's behaviour (which rewrote the monolith with identical content and a new mtime) -- a correctness-equivalent optimisation. Smoke case 3 asserts mtime equality.

Orchestrator brief listed `# TODO move to shared helper` for duplicating _dedup_safely. Implementation documents the duplication inline (compact.py module docstring item 7 + a comment on the DEDUP_KEYS block). `_atomic_write_monolith` and the module-level `_dedup_safely` in raw_vault.py are now unused dead code; I left them in place to keep the edit surgical (orchestrator pinned 'ONLY the body of _compact_small_hub' as the allowed change surface). Flagged in RISKS.
spec_gaps_resolved: Brief silent on the 'no monolith + empty new_frames' case. Implemented to still write an empty monolith (matches the T-08 inline stub's behaviour so downstream readers that stat() the file keep passing).

Brief silent on circular-import protection between raw_vault <-> compact. Implemented as a function-body import inside _compact_small_hub so the top-level import graph in raw_vault.py stays unchanged.

Brief silent on whether _dedup_safely's object round-trip clobbers icao24's 'string' dtype on the way out. _atomic_write explicitly recasts icao24 to 'string' before pyarrow write. Smoke case 6 asserts the round-trip.

integration_points.reads: <out_dir>/<name>/part.parquet (existing small-hub monolith when present); the three non-partitioned hub names: hub_aircraft, hub_airport, sat_aircraft_identity
integration_points.writes: <out_dir>/<name>/part.parquet via tmp (.part.parquet.<pid>.tmp) + os.replace; icao24 cast back to pandas 'string' dtype before the write
consumers: etl4/vault/marts.py (T-14) reads these monoliths via vault_io.read_table

risks: etl4/vault/raw_vault.py now has two unreferenced symbols: _atomic_write_monolith (lines 94-110) and _dedup_safely (lines 300-317). Intentionally left in place to keep the T-09 edit scope limited to 'the body of _compact_small_hub'. A follow-up cleanup task should remove them.

DEDUP_KEYS in compact.py is a hand-duplicated slice of raw_vault._FINAL_DEDUP. Smoke case 1 guards against drift. Hoisting both into a shared module (e.g. etl4/vault/schema.py) is a candidate follow-up.

Existing-first precedence means a null typecode / registration in an early month permanently masks a later non-null one in sat_aircraft_identity. This predates T-09 (WI-1 contract, preserved by T-11 section E item 3). Noted here for the data engineer.
